sections.title: A Geopolitical Shift in Computation
sections.body: For the last decade, AI computation was centralized in a few massive hubs in the US and Europe. That era is ending. The skyrocketing cost of electricity and grid saturation in these markets has created a 'Great Compute Migration.' High-density workloads (Training and Rendering) are moving to where energy is cheap, green, and abundant. Kenya AI Compute sits at the heart of this shift. We are not just building a local data center; we are building a global export engine for intelligence. As AI becomes embedded in every industry, the demand for 'industrialized computation' will continue to outstrip supply, ensuring that infrastructure assets with locked-in low energy costs—like ours—become the most valuable components of the global digital supply chain. Additional context: the project follows a clear rollout roadmap that aligns low-cost energy, infrastructure reliability, and flexible deployment models. sections.title: Global Market Trends
items: Energy Scarcity: Traditional tech hubs are denying new DC permits due to grid limits.
DePIN Proliferation: Decentralization is democratizing access to enterprise-grade compute.
ESG Mandates: Fortune 500 firms are seeking 'Green Compute' to meet Net Zero goals.
Edge AI: Demand for inference in emerging markets is growing 3x faster than in the West.
Hardware Constraints: GPU availability remains tight, making dedicated facilities more valuable.
